messages:
incident-bot: Pager: High generation latency detected in eu-generation-prod. 5xxs increased and tail latency > 2s  (trigger: p50>2000ms). Paging ops-oncall (maria).

ops-oncall (maria): saw it, joining now. grabbing traces. @raj if you have capacity can you look at routing/replicas?

raj (sre): on it. checking infra and autoscaling logs. any customer-facing incidents yet?

ops-oncall (maria): not sure. Telemetry shows a gradual spike since 08:12 UTC, now 08:21. Affects eu region only. No full 5xx outage, but increased 429s from tokenizer service fallback.

sam (product): @maria can we get an initial severity and comms draft? customers will want ETA.

ops-oncall (maria): initial severity P1 (degraded generation latency impacting some requests). I think we should prepare an initial status page entry and signal customers via statuspage. Draft below, feedback?

emma (comms): dropping in to help wording + cadence. Post initial update now, cadence every 30m. Keep it factual + no speculation.

maria: DRAFT STATUS PAGE COPY (please review):
> Initial update (08:24 UTC) — We are investigating elevated generation latency affecting requests in the EU region. Some customers may experience slower responses or timeouts. Our on-call engineers are actively investigating and implementing mitigations. We will post updates every 30 minutes or as we have new information.

raj (sre): suggest add affected services: generation API + tokenizer fallback. Also note no data loss. Updated: 
> Initial update (08:24 UTC) — We are investigating elevated generation latency in the EU region affecting the generation API and tokenizer fallback, which may cause slower responses or increased errors for affected customers. There is no indication of data loss. On-call engineers are investigating root cause and applying mitigations. Updates every 30 minutes.

emma (comms): language looks good. I'll run this by legal if we mention "data loss" — maybe say "no evidence of data loss"

sam (product): +1. Also include guidance: customers can try switching region to US as a temporary workaround; include link to docs.

maria: good point. adding workaround. Revised draft: 
> Initial update (08:24 UTC) — We are investigating elevated generation latency in the EU region affecting the generation API and tokenizer fallback, which may cause slower responses or increased errors for affected customers. There is no evidence of data loss. On-call engineers are investigating and applying mitigations. As a temporary workaround, customers can use the us region. See: https://redwood.ai/docs/regions. Updates every 30 minutes or as new information becomes available.

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-15T08:25:00Z queued for canary fallback to smaller model (eu-gen-fallback-v2). Approve with /deploy approve.

raj (sre): approving canary fallback now. rolling to canary to reduce pressure on tokenizer.

oncall-2 (leo): taking over for next 30m to watch metrics during canary. @maria handing off.

ops-oncall (maria): handoff complete. leo will monitor and I will prepare the 08:54 update.

leo (oncall-2): seeing CPU spikes on tokenization nodes correlating with the latency. Canary fallback in progress, traffic rerouted 30% to fallback.

emma (comms): posting initial status now. I'll ping once it's live and coordinate the next update.

emma (comms): (posted) Statuspage initial update published at 08:27 UTC. Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/12345 (internal link).

sam (product): flagging big customers that may need targeted notif: @acct-team please prepare direct messages for the top 10 affected.

raj (sre): followup telemetry: token cache eviction rate increased significantly at 08:13 UTC, leading to heavier tokenizer load. Investigating root cause (possible cache corruption or misconfig of TTL).

leo (oncall-2): can we roll a cache clear and controlled restart of tokenizer pool? That would mitigate quickly.

ops-oncall (maria): recommend controlled restart of 3/12 tokenizer pods in eu to avoid full pool restart. Raj + Leo coordinate.

raj (sre): restarting 3 pods now. watching error rates.

deploy-bot: Rollout started: tokenizer-eu-restart (3 pods).

leo (oncall-2): after restart, tail latency dipped ~40% within 2 minutes. 429s back down to baseline. Continuing to monitor.

sam (product): great. let's prep the 08:54 update to say mitigation in progress and partial recovery. Emma can you draft?

emma (comms): DRAFT 08:54 UPDATE: 
> Update (08:54 UTC) — We have implemented mitigations (controlled restart of tokenizer pods and canary fallback to a lighter generation model) which have reduced tail latency in the EU region. Some customers may still experience intermittent delays while we monitor. We are continuing root cause analysis. No evidence of data loss. We will publish another update at 09:24 UTC or sooner if we have new information.

maria: LGTM. @raj can you add a brief note for the post-incident RCA about cache TTL and recent config changes?

raj (sre): yes — there's a config sync that rolled at 08:10 that adjusted token-cache TTLs. adding to RCA notes.

emma (comms): publishing 08:54 update now.

emma (comms): (posted) Statuspage update published at 08:55 UTC.

leo (oncall-2): metrics stable for 10 minutes. lowering severity to P2 for internal tracking, keeping public status as Major Degradation until fully recovered.

sam (product): ok prepare resolved notice template when we confirm stable for 30 minutes. Emma, I'll need copy for postmortem customer summary too.

emma (comms): will draft resolved notice and a short customer-friendly RCA summary.

ops-oncall (maria): handing back oncall to leo — I'll join RCA meeting in 30. Good job team.

incident-bot: Incident incident-12345 assigned to teams: SRE, Product, Comms.

emma (comms): RESOLVED DRAFT (placeholder): 
> Resolved (09:30 UTC) — The elevated generation latency in the EU region has been resolved. Mitigations including controlled tokenizer pod restarts and a canary fallback deployment reduced tail latency and error rates. We are continuing to investigate the root cause (a recent token-cache configuration change is under review). There is no evidence of customer data loss. If you are still experiencing issues, please contact support.

raj (sre): confirm metrics show sustained baseline for 25 minutes now. If remain stable 5 more minutes we can publish resolved.

leo (oncall-2): metrics at baseline 31 minutes. publishing resolved now.

emma (comms): (posted) Resolved notice published at 09:32 UTC. Customer summary & RCA to follow in next 24-48h.

sam (product): thanks everyone. I'll compile the top-level customer note with the RCA once we have the full timeline and root cause.

maria: adding final notes to incident doc. closing thread.
